children.name: Antrostomus
children.description: The New World nightjars formerly lumped in Caprimulgus but now separated based on molecular and morphological evidence. Antrostomus comprises roughly 15 species distributed from Canada south through the Caribbean and Central America to South America, including the iconic Eastern Whip-poor-will. Several species have extremely restricted ranges and are poorly known.

children.name: Antrostomus anthonyi
children.description: A recently described species from dry forest in coastal Ecuador and Peru, separated from the Rufous Nightjar on the basis of vocalizations and morphology. Named for the American collector Alfred Webster Anthony, it inhabits dry deciduous forest in the Tumbesian region — one of the world's most threatened biodiversity hotspots. Its small range warrants careful conservation monitoring.

children.name: Antrostomus arizonae
children.description: The Mexican whip-poor-will, (Antrostomus arizonae), is a medium-sized nightjar of the southwestern United States, Mexico, and northern Central America.

children.name: Antrostomus badius
children.description: The Yucatan nightjar (Antrostomus badius) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Antrostomus carolinensis
children.description: The chuck-will's-widow (Antrostomus carolinensis) is a nocturnal bird of the nightjar family Caprimulgidae. It is mostly found in the southeastern United States (with disjunct populations in Long Island, New York; Ontario, Canada; and Cape Cod, Massachusetts) near swamps, rocky uplands, and pine woods. It migrates to the West Indies, Central America, and northwestern South America.

children.name: Antrostomus cubanensis
children.description: The Cuban nightjar (Antrostomus cubanensis), sometimes also Greater Antillean nightjar, is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Antrostomus ekmani
children.description: The Hispaniolan nightjar (Antrostomus ekmani) is a nightjar species endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola, which is shared by the Dominican Republic and Haiti..

children.name: Antrostomus nigrescens
children.description: A dark, soot-brown nightjar of the Guiana Highlands and adjacent lowlands, occupying rocky outcrops, tepui slopes, and adjacent forest. Its nearly uniform blackish-brown plumage sets it apart from all other South American nightjars and makes it extremely difficult to spot on a dark rock surface. It is often detected by its sharp, high-pitched call.

children.name: Antrostomus noctitherus
children.description: The Puerto Rican nightjar, Puerto Rican whip-poor-will or guabairo (Antrostomus noctitherus) is a bird in the nightjar family found in the coastal dry scrub forests in localized areas of southwestern Puerto Rico. It was described in 1916 from bones found in a cave in north central Puerto Rico and a single skin specimen from 1888, and was considered extinct until observed in the wild in 1961. The current population is estimated as 1,400-2,000 mature birds. The species is currently classified as Endangered due to pressures from habitat loss.

children.name: Antrostomus ridgwayi
children.description: The buff-collared nightjar or Ridgway's whip-poor-will (Antrostomus ridgwayi) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and the U.S. State of Arizona.

children.name: Antrostomus rufus
children.description: The rufous nightjar (Antrostomus rufus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Antrostomus salvini
children.description: The tawny-collared nightjar (Antrostomus salvini) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is endemic to Mexico.

children.name: Antrostomus saturatus
children.description: The dusky nightjar or dusky whip-poor-will (Antrostomus saturatus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Antrostomus sericeus
children.description: A poorly known nightjar of the Amazon Basin, favouring terra firme forest and forest edge in the lowlands east of the Andes from Colombia south to Bolivia and east to northern Brazil. Its white outer tail feathers, which appear silky in the hand, give the species its common name. It is encountered infrequently and details of its breeding biology remain undescribed.

children.name: Antrostomus sericocaudatus
children.description: The silky-tailed nightjar (Antrostomus sericocaudatus) is a species of nightjar birds in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Antrostomus vociferus
children.description: The eastern whip-poor-will (Antrostomus vociferus; also called "whip-o-will", "whip o' will", etc.) is a medium-sized () bird within the nightjar family, Caprimulgidae, from North America.

children.name: Asio
children.description: Asio - a genus in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Asio fasciata
children.description: Asio fasciata is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Asio spilogaster
children.description: Asio spilogaster is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Caprimulgus
children.description: The largest nightjar genus, spanning Africa, Europe, and Asia with about 35 species. Masters of cryptic plumage, they roost motionless on the forest floor or along branches by day, invisible among dead leaves. At dusk they fill the air with churring, trilling, or whistling songs and hawk moths and beetles in a wide rictal-bristled gape.

children.name: Caprimulgus aegypius
children.description: Caprimulgus aegypius is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Caprimulgus aegyptius
children.description: The Egyptian nightjar (Caprimulgus aegyptius) is a medium-small nightjar which occurs in south west Asia and north Africa and winters in tropical Africa.

children.name: Caprimulgus affinis
children.description: The savanna nightjar (Caprimulgus affinis), also known as allied nightjar or Franklin's nightjar, is a species of nightjar found in South and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Caprimulgus andamanicus
children.description: The Andaman nightjar (Caprimulgus andamanicus) is a species of nightjar found in the Andaman Islands..

children.name: Caprimulgus asiaticus
children.description: The Indian nightjar (Caprimulgus asiaticus) is a small nightjar which is a resident breeder in open lands across South Asia and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Caprimulgus atripennis
children.description: Jerdon's nightjar (Caprimulgus atripennis) is a medium-sized nightjar species native to southern India and Sri Lanka. Formerly considered as a subspecies of the long-tailed nightjar, it is best recognized by its distinctive call which sounds like a wooden plank being beaten periodically with each note ending in a quaver. The common name commemorates Thomas C. Jerdon who described the species.

children.name: Caprimulgus batesi
children.description: Bates's nightjar (Caprimulgus batesi) or the forest nightjar, is a bird species of the family Caprimulgidae, native to the Congolian rainforests.

children.name: Caprimulgus celebensis
children.description: The Sulawesi nightjar (Caprimulgus celebensis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Caprimulgus centralasicus
children.description: The European nightjar (Caprimulgus europaeus), common goatsucker, Eurasian nightjar or just nightjar is a crepuscular and nocturnal bird in the nightjar family that breeds across most of Europe and the Palearctic to Mongolia and Northwestern China.

children.name: Caprimulgus clarus
children.description: The slender-tailed nightjar (Caprimulgus clarus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in parts of eastern and central Africa, including the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

children.name: Caprimulgus climacurus
children.description: The long-tailed nightjar (Caprimulgus climacurus) is one of 98 species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae, the "true nightjars". It is a nocturnal, insectivorous bird characterized by its distinctive long tail. It is found throughout mainland Africa in open areas, arid semi-deserts, and savannas, with common sightings alongside roadways.

children.name: Caprimulgus concretus
children.description: Bonaparte's nightjar (Caprimulgus concretus), also known as the Sunda nightjar, is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is native to the islands of Sumatra, Belitung and Borneo. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Caprimulgus donaldsoni
children.description: Donaldson Smith's nightjar (Caprimulgus donaldsoni) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Tanzania. It was named in honor of the 19th-century American explorer Arthur Donaldson Smith.

children.name: Caprimulgus egresius
children.description: A little-known nightjar endemic to Pemba Island off the coast of Tanzania in the Indian Ocean. It was long treated as a subspecies of the Natal Nightjar before being recognized as a distinct island endemic. Given the restricted area of Pemba Island and ongoing forest loss, its population is considered small and potentially vulnerable.

children.name: Caprimulgus europaeus
children.description: The European nightjar, common goatsucker, Eurasian nightjar or just nightjar is a crepuscular and nocturnal bird in the nightjar family that breeds across most of Europe and the Palearctic to Mongolia and Northwestern China. The Latin generic name refers to the old myth that the nocturnal nightjar suckled from goats, causing them to cease to give milk. The six subspecies differ clinally, the birds becoming smaller and paler towards the east of the range.

children.name: Caprimulgus eximius
children.description: The golden nightjar (Caprimulgus eximius) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Caprimulgus fossii
children.description: The square-tailed nightjar (Caprimulgus fossii) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae which is native to tropical and subtropical woodlands of the Afrotropics. It has an extensive range south of the African equator. Despite not having a completely "square tail", its naming highlights a distinguishing field mark. The similarly plumaged slender-tailed nightjar, found in dry bush country of the tropics, differs namely by its protruding central tail feathers. It is alternatively known as the Gabon nightjar or Gaboon nightjar or the Mozambique nightjar.

children.name: Caprimulgus fraenatus
children.description: The sombre nightjar or dusky nightjar (Caprimulgus fraenatus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Caprimulgus indicus
children.description: The jungle nightjar (Caprimulgus indicus) is a species of nightjar found in the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Caprimulgus inornatus
children.description: The plain nightjar (Caprimulgus inornatus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Caprimulgus jotaka
children.description: The grey nightjar (Caprimulgus jotaka; also "gray" in some non-local literature) is a species of nightjar found in East Asia, breeding from southeastern Russia south through China, the Korean Peninsula and Japan to northern Indochina and westward along the Himalayas.

children.name: Caprimulgus longipennis
children.description: The standard-winged nightjar (Caprimulgus longipennis) is a nocturnal bird in the nightjar family. Previously placed with the pennant-winged nightjar (Caprimulgus vexillarius) in their own genus, Macrodipteryx, it is native to Africa and displays extreme sexual dimorphism. During the breeding season, males will grow broad ornamental flight feathers longer than their body.

children.name: Caprimulgus macrurus
children.description: The large-tailed nightjar (Caprimulgus macrurus) is a species of nightjar known for its distinctive long, broad tail and cryptic plumage that allows it to blend into its surroundings..

children.name: Caprimulgus madagascariensis
children.description: The Madagascar nightjar or Madagascan nightjar (Caprimulgus madagascariensis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Caprimulgus mahrattensis
children.description: The Sykes's nightjar, Sykes' nightjar, Sind nightjar or Sindh nightjar (Caprimulgus mahrattensis) is a nightjar species found in northwestern South Asia. This species has a large range with stable population size and therefore has been listed as "Least Concern" with no prediction of substantial human influence on their habitats in the near future.

children.name: Caprimulgus mandevillei
children.description: A distinctively patterned nightjar of the humid forests of eastern Madagascar, formerly treated as a subspecies of the Madagascar Nightjar but now recognized as a full species based on plumage and vocal differences. It shows a well-defined pale collar separating the dark crown from the streaked back. Its humid forest habitat is under threat from clearance and slash-and-burn agriculture.

children.name: Caprimulgus manillensis
children.description: The Philippine nightjar (Caprimulgus manillensis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Caprimulgus meesi
children.description:
Mees's nightjar (Caprimulgus meesi) is a member of the nightjar family (Caprimulgidae) described as new to science in 2004.
It is a representative of the large-tailed nightjar complex found on Flores and Sumba, Indonesia. Previously unrecognised as a separate taxon due to its lack of morphological distinctness, Sangster and Rozendaal (2004) described this new species on the basis of its vocalisations, which differ significantly from those of the large-tailed nightjar races resident on other islands in the Lesser Sundas.

children.name: Caprimulgus monticolus
children.description: The savanna nightjar (Caprimulgus affinis), also known as allied nightjar or Franklin's nightjar, is a species of nightjar found in South and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Caprimulgus natalensis
children.description: The swamp nightjar or Natal nightjar (Caprimulgus natalensis) is a crepuscular and nocturnal bird in the nightjar family found in Africa.

children.name: Caprimulgus nigriscapularis
children.description: The fiery-necked nightjar (Caprimulgus pectoralis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae, which is found mostly in Africa south of the equator, though it has been spotted in a few countries north of the equator. It is most often found in woodland savannas or other deciduous woodlands. It is usually distinguished by its tawny coloured collar which gives the species its common name. It has a distinctive call that many have rendered as 'good-lord-deliver-us'. The fiery-necked nightjar is an insectivorous species that mostly eats butterflies, moths and other insects. The fiery-necked nightjar breeds after the dry season and typically produce two clutches with two eggs per clutch.

children.name: Caprimulgus novaehollandiae
children.description: Caprimulgus novaehollandiae is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Caprimulgus nubicus
children.description: The Nubian nightjar (Caprimulgus nubicus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Caprimulgus pectoralis
children.description: The fiery-necked nightjar (Caprimulgus pectoralis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae, which is found mostly in Africa south of the equator, though it has been spotted in a few countries north of the equator. It is most often found in woodland savannas or other deciduous woodlands. It is usually distinguished by its tawny coloured collar which gives the species its common name. It has a distinctive call that many have rendered as 'good-lord-deliver-us'. The fiery-necked nightjar is an insectivorous species that mostly eats butterflies, moths and other insects. The fiery-necked nightjar breeds after the dry season and typically produce two clutches with two eggs per clutch.

children.name: Caprimulgus phalaena
children.description: The Palau nightjar (Caprimulgus phalaena) is a species of nightjar endemic to Palau..

children.name: Caprimulgus piurensis
children.description: Caprimulgus piurensis (nightjar) is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Caprimulgus poliocephalus
children.description: The montane nightjar (Caprimulgus poliocephalus), mountain nightjar or Abyssinian nightjar, is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Caprimulgus prigoginei
children.description:
Prigogine's nightjar (Caprimulgus prigoginei) or the Itombwe nightjar, is a bird species of tropical central Africa. It is known from only one specimen taken at Malenge in the Itombwe Mountains in Belgian Congo in August 1955.
It appears to be a forest species, but nothing is known of its habits or breeding, although it is likely to nest on bare ground like its relatives. It is assumed to be a nocturnal insectivore like other nightjars.

children.name: Caprimulgus pulchellus
children.description: Salvadori's nightjar (Caprimulgus pulchellus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Caprimulgus ramsayi
children.description: A seldom-observed nightjar of the eastern Himalayas, southern China, and mainland Southeast Asia, inhabiting montane broadleaf forest and scrub at moderate elevations. It is a sombre, darkly marked bird compared with the more patterned congeners it associates with in the region. Its vocalizations and habits are poorly documented in the literature.

children.name: Caprimulgus ruficollis
children.description: The red-necked nightjar (Caprimulgus ruficollis) is the largest of the nightjars occurring in Europe. It breeds in Iberia and North Africa, and winters in tropical West Africa.

children.name: Caprimulgus rufigena
children.description: The rufous-cheeked nightjar (Caprimulgus rufigena) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is an intra-African migrant that breeds in the south of its range. It spends the non-breeding season in eastern Nigeria, Cameroon, southern Chad and Sudan, the Republic of the Congo, the D.R.C. And western Central African Republic. Throughout the year it can be found in Southern Africa. It is a nocturnal species that feeds on flying insects, mainly hunting at dusk and the early night. They can hunt at night thanks to their large eyes that are adept at seeing in the dark. They cannot see in complete darkness and most likely cannot see colours either. The rufous-cheeked nightjar forms monogamous pairs and the egg laying period is from September to November. It looks very similar to other African nightjars and they are frequently misidentified during research and studies.

children.name: Caprimulgus ruwenzorii
children.description: The montane nightjar (Caprimulgus poliocephalus), mountain nightjar or Abyssinian nightjar, is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Caprimulgus solala
children.description: The Nechisar nightjar (Caprimulgus solala) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Caprimulgus stellatus
children.description:
The star-spotted nightjar (Caprimulgus stellatus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in central Ethiopia, northern and northwestern Kenya and southern South Sudan.
Star-spotted nightjar tend to inhabit low-altitude and dry habitats such as the lava-strewn fields, stony or sandy semi-deserts, drawf grassland as well as open bushland.

children.name: Caprimulgus tristigma
children.description: The freckled nightjar or freckled rock nightjar (Caprimulgus tristigma) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Caprimulgus vexillarius
children.description: The pennant-winged nightjar (Caprimulgus vexillarius) is a species of nightjar that occurs from Nigeria to northern South Africa. It is an intra-African migrant and displays remarkable sexual dimorphism in the breeding season.

children.name: Eleothreptus
children.description: A small genus of two South American nightjars with unusual wing shapes — one has sickle-shaped outer primaries and the other has greatly expanded inner primaries in the male. Both are closely associated with wetland edges and open grasslands of the southern cone.

children.name: Eleothreptus anomalus
children.description: The sickle-winged nightjar (Eleothreptus anomalus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and possibly Uruguay.

children.name: Eleothreptus candicans
children.description: The white-winged nightjar (Eleothreptus candicans) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil and Paraguay.

children.name: Eurostopodus
children.description: Seven species of nightjars ranging from South and Southeast Asia through New Guinea and Australia. They tend to be larger than most Caprimulgus species and occupy a variety of habitats from rainforest to open woodland. Several species have elaborate ear-like head tufts and bright eye-shine. The genus is the main nightjar radiation in Australasia.

children.name: Eurostopodus archboldi
children.description:
Archbold's nightjar (Eurostopodus archboldi), also known as the mountain eared-nightjar or cloud-forest nightjar, is a dark and densely spotted species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is endemic to New Guinea and is the only nightjar species inhabiting the high-elevation subtropical and tropical montane forests of New Guinea. This bird is named after the American explorer Richard Archbold, whose expedition in New Guinea in 1933-1934 led to the discovery of the species.
Archbold's nightjar is a nocturnal species, roosting on the ground during the day and emerging to forage at night. E. Archboldi is a proficient hunter, specialized in catching large insects while in flight.

children.name: Eurostopodus argus
children.description: The spotted nightjar or spotted eared-nightjar (Eurostopodus argus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Eurostopodus diabolicus
children.description: The Satanic nightjar (Eurostopodus diabolicus), also Heinrich's nightjar, The species was discovered in 1931 by Gerd Heinrich, a German natural historian who collected a single female holotype from Mount Klabat on the Minahasa peninsula of Northern Sulawesi.

children.name: Eurostopodus exul
children.description: The New Caledonian nightjar (Eurostopodus exul) is a poorly known species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Eurostopodus macrotis
children.description: Eurostopodus macrotis (Great Eared Nightjar) is a nightjars species found in Asia region.

children.name: Eurostopodus mystacalis
children.description: The white-throated nightjar or white-throated eared-nightjar (Eurostopodus mystacalis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is endemic to eastern Australia; it is a non-breeding winter visitor in Papua New Guinea. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forests.

children.name: Eurostopodus nigripennis
children.description: The Solomons nightjar (Eurostopodus nigripennis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Eurostopodus papuensis
children.description: The Papuan nightjar or Papuan eared-nightjar (Eurostopodus papuensis) is a species of nightjar in the family of Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Eurostopodus temminckii
children.description: The Malaysian eared nightjar or Malay eared nightjar (Lyncornis temminckii) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It was formerly placed in the genus Eurostopodus. It is known as Taptibau Kecil in Bahasa melayu or Tukang Tabtibau amongst Malaysian indigenous communities. It is dispersed throughout Southeast Asia, primarily occurring in Malaysia, Sumatra, Borneo, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore. It is a nocturnal insectivorous bird characterised by cryptic colouration of brown and white patterns, to aid it in camouflaging into its environment. Due to the nocturnal nature and feeding habits, it prefers subtropical, tropical and moist lowland forests, and have been recorded from sea-level to 1065 meters. It is easily distinguished by its 'ear-tufts,' giving it an "eared" appearance which led to its name.

children.name: Gactornis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Collared Nightjar of Madagascar. It is one of the most distinctive nightjars on the island, characterized by a bold pale collar and large size relative to other Malagasy nightjars. Its affinities lie with the Afro-Asian nightjar radiation.

children.name: Gactornis enarratus
children.description: The collared nightjar (Gactornis enarratus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: "Hydropsalis torquata"
children.description: "Hydropsalis torquata" is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Lurocalis
children.description: Two species of stocky, short-tailed nightjars that replace most other nightjars in the forest canopy, hunting insects in swift aerial sallies above and just below the canopy rather than from the ground. They have relatively long, pointed wings compared with other nightjars and are fast, agile fliers.

children.name: Lurocalis semitorquatus
children.description: The short-tailed nighthawk (Lurocalis semitorquatus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Mexico, in every Central American country except El Salvador, in Trinidad and Tobago, and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

children.name: Lurocalis rufiventris
children.description: The rufous-bellied nighthawk (Lurocalis rufiventris), sometimes also Taczanowski's nighthawk, is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

children.name: Lurocalis nattereri
children.description: Lurocalis nattereri is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Lyncornis
children.description: Three large, eared nightjars of South and Southeast Asia, allied with Eurostopodus but sufficiently distinct to warrant their own genus. They are birds of forest interiors and forest edge in tropical Asia. The Large-tailed Nightjar is the most widespread and best-known species.

children.name: Lyncornis cerviniceps
children.description: The most widespread and frequently encountered nightjar in Southeast Asia, ranging from northeast India through Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, and the Malay Peninsula to the Philippines and Sulawesi. A common bird of forest edges, secondary growth, cultivated land, and even well-wooded gardens in cities, it is often the nightjar most people in Asia first encounter. Its repetitive 'chonk' call rings through tropical nights.

children.name: Lyncornis macrotis
children.description: The great eared nightjar (Lyncornis macrotis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in southwest India and in parts of Southeast Asia. This very large nightjar has long barred wings, a barred tail and long ear-tufts which are often recumbent. It has a white throat band but has no white on its wings or on its tail.

children.name: Lyncornis macrurus
children.description: A medium-large nightjar of the Sundaic lowland rainforests of the Malay Peninsula, Borneo, and Sumatra, inhabiting both primary forest and forest edge. Its loud, slightly mournful 'kwok' call is characteristic of Bornean and Sumatran forests at night. Deforestation has reduced its habitat considerably and it is now uncommon across much of its range.

children.name: Lyncornis temminckii
children.description: The Malaysian eared nightjar or Malay eared nightjar (Lyncornis temminckii) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Macropsalis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing one of the most striking nightjars of the South American highlands. The genus name refers to the enormous, forceps-like tail of the male. It inhabits montane grassland and forest edge in the Atlantic Forest region of southeastern Brazil and adjacent Argentina.

children.name: Macropsalis forcipata
children.description: Macropsalis forcipata (Long-trained Nightjar) is a nightjars species found in South America region.

children.name: Macropsalis creagra
children.description: Macropsalis creagra is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Nyctidromus
children.description: A small genus of two large-eyed, long-tailed nightjars of the Neotropics and southern North America. They are among the more terrestrial nightjars, often running along roads and forest paths at night with glowing red eye-shine. Males perform elaborate wing-spreading display dances to court females.

children.name: Nyctidromus albicollis
children.description: The pauraque (Nyctidromus albicollis) - also called the common pauraque to distinguish it from similar species - is a nightjar species, one of two birds in the genus Nyctidromus. It breeds in the subtropical and tropical regions of the New World, and except for northernmost birds it is largely resident all year round.

children.name: Nyctidromus anthonyi
children.description: Anthony's nightjar (Nyctidromus anthonyi), also known as the scrub nightjar, is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

children.name: Nyctidromus hirundinaceus
children.description: Nyctidromus hirundinaceus is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Nyctidromus nigrescens
children.description: Nyctidromus nigrescens is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Nyctiphrynus
children.description: Four species of small, round-winged, forest-floor nightjars endemic to the forests of Mexico, Central America, and the Pacific coast of Colombia. They are less vocal than many relatives and are seldom recorded away from their favoured dense forest habitats. Several species have very restricted ranges.

children.name: Nyctiphrynus ocellatus
children.description: The ocellated poorwill (Nyctiphrynus ocellatus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Nyctiphrynus yucatanicus
children.description: The Yucatan poorwill (Nyctiphrynus yucatanicus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Nyctiphrynus rosenbergi
children.description: The Chocó poorwill (Nyctiphrynus rosenbergi) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

children.name: Nyctiphrynus mcleodii
children.description: The eared poorwill (Nyctiphrynus mcleodii) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Nyctipolus
children.description: Two species of small South American nightjars recently separated from Caprimulgus on molecular grounds, occupying the rocky outcrops and forest edges of the Guiana region and northeastern Brazil. They are compact birds with short tails and prefer elevated rocky terrain to the forest floor.

children.name: Nyctipolus nigrescens
children.description: Nyctipolus nigrescens (Blackish Nightjar) is a nightjars species found in South America region.

children.name: Nyctipolus hirundinaceus
children.description: The pygmy nightjar (Nyctipolus hirundinaceus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Nyctipolus maculosus
children.description: Nyctipolus maculosus is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Nyctiprogne
children.description: Two small, swift-flying South American nightjars closely associated with large rivers and their sandy margins. They forage at low altitude over water in fast, swallow-like flight and roost on sandbars and rock outcrops in rivers. Nyctiprogne is one of the more aquatically associated nightjar genera.

children.name: Nyctiprogne leucopyga
children.description: The band-tailed nighthawk (Nyctiprogne leucopyga) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is widely spread throughout northern and central South America. Five subspecies are recognised. They are nocturnal birds that feed on flying insects. As with almost all nightjars, they lay their eggs directly on the ground and rely their camouflaged plumage to avoid predation.

children.name: Nyctiprogne vieilliardi
children.description: The plain-tailed nighthawk (Nyctiprogne vielliardi) is a species of nightjar (probably least known of the nightjars) in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Nyctiprogne vielliardi
children.description: The plain-tailed nighthawk (Nyctiprogne vielliardi) is a species of nightjar (probably least known of the nightjars) in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Nyctiprogne viellioti
children.description: A closely related species to the Band-winged Nightjar, formerly considered conspecific but now treated as distinct based on plumage and range differences. Named for the prolific French ornithologist Louis Jean Pierre Vieillot, it inhabits river-edge habitats in the Guiana Shield region and coastal northeastern South America. Like its congener, it forages in swift, low flights over water.

children.name: Phalaenoptilus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Common Poorwill, the only bird known to enter extended torpor (hibernation) in winter. Found across western North America in arid and semi-arid scrubland, this small nightjar is notable for its ability to lower its body temperature dramatically and survive weeks without food.

children.name: Phalaenoptilus nuttallii
children.description: The common poorwill (Phalaenoptilus nuttallii) is a nocturnal bird of the family Caprimulgidae, the nightjars.

children.name: Podager
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Nacunda Nighthawk, the largest nighthawk in South America. It inhabits open grasslands and savanna from Panama to Argentina and, unlike most nightjars, is active well into daylight hours, soaring high in loose flocks to hawk insects.

children.name: Podager nacunda
children.description: The nacunda nighthawk (Chordeiles nacunda) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Setopagis
children.description: A genus of small to medium South American nightjars characterized by moderately long tails and relatively plain, cryptic plumage. The genus was resurrected when molecular studies confirmed that several species formerly placed in Caprimulgus or Hydropsalis formed a distinct Neotropical lineage. Members inhabit grasslands, forest edge, and riparian scrub across South America.

children.name: Setopagis cayennensis
children.description: A common nightjar of open lowland habitats from Trinidad and the Lesser Antilles south through coastal South America to Argentina. Males are strikingly marked with large white tail and wing patches that flash conspicuously in display flights at dusk. It is one of the most frequently encountered nightjars across much of northern South America.

children.name: Setopagis heterura
children.description: Todd's nightjar (Setopagis heterura) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Setopagis heterurus
children.description: Todd's nightjar (Setopagis heterura) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, and Venezuela.

children.name: Setopagis maculicaudus
children.description: A small nightjar with distinctive white spots on the outer tail feathers, found patchily from southern Mexico south through Central America and into western South America. It inhabits open grassland, savanna, and cerrado, and is often found in areas with scattered scrub and tall grass. Its sharp 'tik-tik-tik' call is more likely to attract attention than its cryptic plumage.

children.name: Setopagis maculosa
children.description: The Cayenne nightjar (Setopagis maculosa) is a species of bird in the nightjar family only known from a single specimen, a male taken on the Fleuve Mana, French Guiana, in 1917..

children.name: Setopagis parvula
children.description: The little nightjar (Setopagis parvula) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Setopagis parvulus
children.description: The little nightjar (Setopagis parvula) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Setopagis whitelyi
children.description: The Roraiman nightjar (Tepuiornis whitelyi) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Siphonorhis
children.description: Two species of Caribbean nightjars, one of which — the Jamaican Poorwill — was believed extinct for over a century before being rediscovered. Both are small, forest-floor nightjars of island habitats that have suffered greatly from introduced predators and habitat loss.

children.name: Siphonorhis americana
children.description: The Jamaican poorwill (Siphonorhis americana), also known as the Jamaican pauraque or Jamaican least pauraque, is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae..

children.name: Siphonorhis americanus
children.description: The Jamaican poorwill (Siphonorhis americana), also known as the Jamaican pauraque or Jamaican least pauraque, is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

children.name: Siphonorhis brewsteri
children.description: The least poorwill or least pauraque (Siphonorhis brewsteri) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae, and the only confirmed extant species of its genus.

children.name: Siphonorhis daiquiri
children.description: Siphonorhis daiquiri is a caprimulgidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Systellura longirostris

children.name: Systellura roraimae
children.description: Systellura roraimae (Tepui Nightjar) is a caprimulgidae species found in South America region.

children.name: Uropsalis
children.description: Two Andean nightjars famed for the extraordinary tail streamers of the males, which are among the longest relative to body size of any bird in the world. They inhabit montane forest edges, rocky Andean slopes, and grass-filled valleys at elevations from 1,500 to 3,500 m.

children.name: Uropsalis segmentata
children.description: The swallow-tailed nightjar (Uropsalis segmentata) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Uropsalis lyra
children.description: The lyre-tailed nightjar (Uropsalis lyra) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
